      <section id="welcome" class="home-hero">
        <h1>AffineDrift</h1>
        <p class="home-hero__subtitle">Scientific Notes on Golf Mechanics, Modeling, and Control</p>
        <p class="home-hero__lede">
          AffineDrift is a technical research portfolio on golf swing mechanics, multibody dynamics, and nonlinear control. It collects textbook-style chapters, source maps, reproducible model links, validation notes, and critique responses so claims can be read with their assumptions and evidence in view.
        </p>
      </section>

      <!-- Core framework -->
      <section id="framework" class="home-framework">
        <h2>The Core Framework</h2>
        <p>Several pages model the golf swing as a control-affine system:</p>
        <div class="math-showcase">
          $$\dot{x} = f(x) + g(x)u$$
        </div>
        <p>
          Where <em>f(x)</em> represents the drift dynamics (passive forces including gravity and velocity-dependent inertial coupling terms) and <em>g(x)u</em> represents the controlled torque inputs from the golfer.
        </p>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <strong>Provenance.</strong> The control-affine form ẋ = f(x) + g(x)u is standard in nonlinear control theory (Isidori, 1995; Nijmeijer &amp; van der Schaft, 1990). Its application to golf biomechanics — the drift/input decomposition, ZTCF, and DCR — is AffineDrift synthesis. See <a href="articles/theory-part1.html">Theory Part 1</a> for the derivation and <a href="critiques/index.html">Critiques &amp; Responses</a> for scope limitations.
        </aside>
      </section>
